prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one original portrait illustration of Jackie Leven around 1994–1995, for a coherent series of restrained dark dry-brush portraits spanning his life.

INPUT ROLES AND PRIORITY:
Image 1 is the PRIMARY PERIOD REFERENCE, a blurry monochrome photograph supplied for 1994–95. It determines the apparent period, wavy medium-length hairstyle, approximate head shape and build, dark jacket and open shirt, and thoughtful alert character. Interpret the person, do not reproduce the blur, hand-under-chin pose, room, table or other people.
Image 2 is an EARLIER ORIGINAL photograph (1983), with Jackie the man on the right. Use only as a supporting anchor for his individual facial structure. Do not reproduce the woman, cover design, younger lean physique or long slicked-back hairstyle.
Image 3 is a CLEARER LATER ORIGINAL photograph (around 2000), Jackie holding up a glass. This is the best supporting reference for his characteristic eye sockets, thick brows, eyes, nose and mouth geometry. Use these stable identity cues conservatively to interpret the blurry middle-period photo. Do not copy the glass, hand, text, blond-tipped tightly curled hair, tilt, colour or exact photographic composition. The new portrait should appear a little younger and less heavy than this later reference, as supported by image 1, not like the slim young 1983 man.
Image 4 is an APPROVED ILLUSTRATION from the website, an older Jackie with guitar. This is ONLY a style, palette, contrast and edge-treatment reference. Do not use this older man's age, jowls, broad later build, face pose or guitar.
Prioritize the original photographs for identity. This is a middle-period portrait of the SAME recognizable person, not a statistical blend of unrelated generic faces.

SUBJECT:
Jackie in his mid-forties, with the medium-length loose wavy dark hair of image 1, a loose side/near-centre part and a broad lifted wave across the forehead, hair curling around the ears and nape. Distinctive heavy brows, slightly hooded expressive eyes with natural asymmetry, substantial straight nose, characteristic quiet closed mouth and fuller cheeks than in 1983 while retaining a defined jaw. Natural unidealized face; no artificial handsome-model proportions, no heavy ageing, no exaggerated deep wrinkles. Clean-shaven or only a faint natural shadow, no invented moustache or beard. Thoughtful, watchful and self-possessed, no smile.
Use selective expressive marks where the period reference is indistinct; do not invent intricate skin or facial detail.

NEW COMPOSITION:
One vertical 4:5 head-and-upper-chest portrait, entire head and hair comfortably inside the frame. Torso gently turned toward the viewer's right, head almost frontal with a slight turn and gaze just toward the viewer's left. Relaxed grounded shoulders, not a heroic pose. Both hands outside frame; no chin support. Keep the dark jacket and open shirt from image 1, abbreviated to a few rough lapel/collar gestures. Render the shirt in subdued grey, not a bright white triangle. No table, furniture, necklace detail, glass, guitar or other objects. The shoulders, chest and lower jacket dissolve into darkness and sparse dry-brush marks. Dark breathing room around the head.

STYLE:
A drawn dry-brush ink portrait with the exact visual family of image 4: broad quiet matte-grey light/shadow planes, rough broken hand-made strokes, economical directional marks and unworked negative space. Match its level of abstraction, rather than adding photorealistic detail to compensate for the blurry photo. Preserve accurately placed and recognizable eyes, nose, lips and overall anatomy. Hair is grouped into broad wavy masses and sparse gestural strokes, clothes mostly disappear. No smooth digital airbrushing, photoreal skin pores, intricate hair strands, mechanical vector posterization, fine engraving, or glossy uniform embossed paint texture. Organic irregularity in the drawing, no distortions of the face.

PALETTE:
Strictly neutral charcoal and muted cool-neutral grey on near-black anthracite #0d0f12, to fit a dark website. NO brown, sepia, beige, cream or warm cast from the photos, no coloured accents. Same subdued watermark-like presence as image 4: broad facial light planes approximately #61676b to #777c80, sparse accents around #85898c, no bright white. Natural positive lighting, dark pupils, nostrils and mouth within lighter grey forms. Modest directional light makes the face readable without theatrical hard split lighting. Let dark hair and jacket merge into the background.
Outside edges become flat plain anthracite with no frame, paper border or visible rectangle. No text, writing, signature, logo, album artwork or collage. One standalone portrait.
